articleTitle: A Blockchain-based approach to securing data in smart agriculture
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Digital transformation in the socioeconomic sectors has become a requirement in Algeria, particularly in the agricultural field. Modern agriculture is mainly based on new communication technologies such as IoT, 5G and Cloud/Edge computing, where data can be shared quickly and transparently. Ensuring security to access data in this system is a challenge that has always aroused researchers because of the importance of data reliability to make the right decisions for the advancement and development of any sector. Blockchain's various qualities, including smart contracts, decentralisation, transparency, data immutability, data privacy, and a consensus process, make it suitable for securing data and achieving its integrity from alteration and tampering. This paper proposes a Blockchain strategy to improve agriculture data security, integrity, management and sharing performance. The proposed approach works in three steps, collecting raw agricultural data from greenhouses and storing it in Edge. This data is encrypted and uploaded to InterPlanetary File Systems (IPFS). Then, a transaction is generated by the smart contract and stored in the Blockchain network. The approved transaction cannot be modified. Therefore, our system is guaranteed in terms of security and integrity.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm-based Optimal Wireless Sensor Network Deployment
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Many wireless sensor network (WSN) applications have achieved significant advances in sensor node technology. Sensor nodes are able to communicate and sense environmental conditions, however, deploying these nodes can be expensive and dangerous in some cases, which leads to random deployment as the only possible solution. The random deployment may lead to uncovered or unconnected areas, duplicated or missed data, and to waste more energy. Therefore, a Genetic Algorithm (GA) based methodology is implemented for self-organized WSN. In order to implement the process of WSN deployment and ensure low energy consumption, an optimization method is required. Based on the experimental results, GA helps in identifying the best position for each sensor node in order to meet network connectivity and coverage.

articleTitle: Location-based Markov clustering routing protocol versus Density-based clustering routing protocol for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to develop, Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are being utilized more and more. The most pressing issue in these networks is the need to reduce energy consumption as much as possible to ensure the longevity of the network. A novel routing protocol, WMCL-BCRP, has been proposed which is based on Markovian clustering and sensor weighting. It is a hybrid solution that combines the grouping of the network sensors in a centralized way using Markov clustering and the implementation of a new decentralized approach for the election of the cluster heads(CH) and sensors involved in the routing according to two criteria, which are the density of sensors and their residual energy. WMCL-BCRP is an improved version of MCL-BCRP, which utilizes the same clustering system and selects cluster heads, and sends sensors based on their location and energy levels. Simulations of the WMCL-BCRP protocol show significant network lifespan increases compared to its successor MCL-BCRP and LEACH.

articleTitle: Real Time Human Detection by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: One of the most important problems in computer vision and remote sensing is object detection, which identifies particular categories of diverse things in pictures. Two crucial data sources for public security are the thermal infrared (TIR) remote sensing multi-scenario photos and videos produced by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Due to the small scale of the target, complex scene information, low resolution relative to the viewable videos, and dearth of publicly available labeled datasets and training models, their object detection procedure is still difficult. A UAV TIR object detection framework for pictures and videos is suggested in this study. The Forward-looking Infrared (FLIR) cameras used to gather ground-based TIR photos and videos are used to create the “You Only Look Once” (YOLO) model, which is based on CNN architecture. Results indicated that in the validating task, detecting human object had an average precision at 72.5%, using YOLOv7 (YOLO version 7) state of the art model [1], while the detection speed around 161 frames per second (FPS/second). The usefulness of the YOLO architecture is demonstrated in the application, which evaluates the cross-detection performance of people in UAV TIR videos under a YOLOv7 model in terms of the various UAVs' observation angles. The qualitative and quantitative evaluation of object detection from TIR pictures and videos using deep-learning models is supported favorably by this work.

articleTitle: Machine learning Solutions to Model Checking: A Brief Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: During the last decades, artificial intelligence (AI) touched many domains of software engineering. One of them is formal verification (FV), where learning methods could improve the performance of several formal verification approaches. Model checking (MC) is one of the FV techniques used to verify systems. In this article, we investigate the direction of the link between MC and one of AI techniques. We survey several related works about how learning can improve MC in its functionalities. Furthermore, we give an overview of some adapted approaches of ML in MC.

articleTitle: Construction Compressed Quadtree into M-Dimensional Crossed Cubes via the Embedding
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: In parallel computing, an optimal graph embedding is to map nodes and edges of a guest graph onto nodes and paths of a host graph. Quadtrees are an important technique to present spatial based on the principle of recursive decomposition of space. We describe an efficient function to construct a compressed quadtree in crossed cubes topology using embedding technique. Our algorithm takes dilation as principle criteria for determining embedding efficiency.

articleTitle: A CNN based architecture for forgery detection in administrative documents
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The use of digital documents is knowing a widespread in different daily administrative and economic transactions. Simultaneously, the forgery of many documents becomes a crime that costs billions to states and companies. Several researchers tried to develop techniques that automatically detect forged documents using machine learning and image processing. With the immense success of deep learning applications, we employ, in this work, a convolutional neural network architecture that uses a gathered dataset of forged and authentic administrative documents. The results obtained on our dataset of 493 documents reached 73.95% accuracy and 97.3% recall, surpassing the efficiency of the machine learning base methods.

articleTitle: TabNet Based Prediction Model for ICU admission in Covid-19 patients
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is the responsible virus for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). It was reported the first time in Wuhan (China) by late December 2019. The COVID-19 pandemic has become a global health risk due to the urgent need for an Intensive Care Unit (ICU) that exceeded its capacity. To cope with this exponential spread the fast adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and advanced technology is crucial. For this reason, many research works in AI are conducted. In the current paper, we intend to report AI applications and solutions based on machine learning, deep learning, and data mining algorithms for detecting, predicting, and diagnosing COVID-19. Furthermore, this study aims to develop a new deep learning-based method capable of predicting whether a COVID-19 patient requires admission to an intensive care unit using clinical tabular data from Kaggle. This model will contribute to the optimization of ICU resources. The experimental results showed that combining Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and TabNet classifier improved the prediction performance and surpassed the state-of-the-art models: MLP, RF, LR, and KNN.

articleTitle: SAGA Distributed Transactions Verification Using Maude
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Microservices is an architectural style that enables the design of applications as series of services independent from each other in function, maintainability, deployability and scalability. Two phase commit protocol as an example of classical distributed transaction protocols are not suitable for this pattern. These protocols require all participants in a transaction to commit or roll back before the transaction can proceed. This is way saga was chosen to replace 2PC. Saga is a mechanism that belongs to the ‘database per service’ pattern and which guarantees distributed transactions that covers many services. The saga pattern provides transaction management using a sequence of local transactions. Saga can be rolled back by a compensating transaction that ensures one of two possibilities all operations complete successfully or the corresponding compensation transactions are run to undo the change. In this paper, we try to run a verification of saga using the maude language. We use the Saga protocol by orchestration, and we present a verification way to check it.

articleTitle: Parametric Scientific Workflow Scheduling Algorithm in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Scheduling a scientific workflow in a cloud computing environment is one of the most challenging difficulties that researchers face. This is due to the difficulty of having a high-performance scheduler that optimizes cost and time while meeting the demands of the users. In this research, we propose a new Parametric Scheduling Algorithm (PSA) that, depending on the user's needs, reduces the monetary cost, the execution time, or both simultaneously. Our suggested algorithm is based on the Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA) with some modifications and improvements. The WorkflowSim simulator is utilized to compare the performance of our proposed system with the Genetic Algorithm, which is widely used to handle workflow scheduling problems, and the original Slim Mould Algorithm. The simulation results show that our suggested PSA algorithm outperforms the other algorithms.

articleTitle: A SIMD Interpreter for Linear Genetic Programming
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Genetic programming (GP) has been applied as an automatic programming tool to solve various kinds of problems by genetically breeding a population of computer programs using biologically inspired operations. However, it is well known as a computationally demanding approach with a significant potential of parallelization. In this paper, we emphasize parallelizing the evaluation of genetic programs on Graphics Processing Unit (GPU). We used a compact representation for genotypes. This representation is a memory-efficient method that allows efficient evaluation of programs. Our implementation clearly distinguishes between an individual's genotype and phenotype. Thus, the individuals are represented as linear entities (arrays of 32 bits integers) that are decoded and expressed just like nonlinear entities (trees).

articleTitle: WP-CamemBERT for next location Prediction
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: CamemBERT is a Natural Language Processing (NLP) model. The current paper introduced a combination of Bertwordpiece tokenizer and CamemBERT that we named WP-CamemBERT, to solve the next location prediction problem. Substantially, we sought to investigate the performance of our proposed model WP-CamemBERT compared to famous models in the domain that are: Markov, Long-Short Term Memory (LSTMs), Convolutional Neural network (CNN2D), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models. In order to build the next location prediction model, we used a dataset of mobile users made available through the CRAWDAD project. The results showed that WP-Camembert gave significant improvement in the prediction accuracy and surpassed the state of the art models that are: Markov, LSTMs, CNN2D, and SVM. Particularly, WP-CamemBERT enhanced the next location prediction accuracy by at least 3.2%.

articleTitle: A planning framework for QoS based composition services in IoT environment
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Recently, Internet has developed into a new technology known as Internet of Things (IoT), enabling the interconnection of billions sensors, actuators, devices, as well as users, which are applied for huge data generating. Moreover, due to the numerous and heterogeneous included devices, and services delivered, the IoT service discovery, selection, and composition is a challenging task. Given that several services have the same functionality but different non-functional criteria (QoS). Thus it is interesting to create an automatic, dynamic, and optimal IoT service composition system to respond on real time to large scale of services, including QoS. Accordingly, we propose, in this paper, an approach for IoT service composition based automatic planning (AP) enhanced by genetic algorithm (GA). The objective is to produce a plan composition satisfying the optimal QoS. In addition, we employ the cloud technology to establish an optimal IoT service composition with less memory consumption, and expanded scalability of our suggested framework. The simulation results have illustrated the efficiency of our approach to resolve the composition problem in a distributed and dynamic IoT system.

articleTitle: Graph Sampling Aggregators Neural Network for Session-based Recommender System (GS-SBR)
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: In the digital world and competitive digitalization, recommendation systems (RSs) play a significant role in consumers' activities, and intelligent decision. Recently, a new recommendation system, called the Session-Based Recommendation (SBR), presents a product to the user through a session without resorting to personal information. SBRs are applied in various areas. Many recently published scientific papers on SBR are based on GNNs. In the study, We introduce (GS-SBR), a new SBR that uses the Graph Sampling Aggregator (GraphSAGE) that outperforms numerous state-of-the-art efforts.

articleTitle: Digital Waste Collection Monitoring: Biskra City a Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Waste overflow is the primary factor in land pollution. It can cause a variety of adverse health outcomes and increases the risk of respiratory infections, heart disease, and lung cancer, and creates an unsanitary environment. In this paper, a waste monitoring system is proposed for the collecting and handling of waste, as well as a quality of life improvement for citizens that can interact with the system for a better environment. The proposed system consists of three actors: a web application for the administrator, a mobile application for the truck driver, and a mobile application for citizens.

articleTitle: The Multi Agent Nets Architecture as Base for Modelling Smart Home for Elderly
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: With the miniaturization of computer components and sensors, as well as the multiplication of communications capabilities, computing is experiencing major changes paving the way for the era of ambient intelligence. Among the central characteristics of an ambient system, is the context awareness. It allows services to adapt to a user's needs without a need of clarification. Moreover, among the general population really interested by the development of this technology are elderlies with reduced autonomy. The number of this type of person is constantly increasing. Placing these people in hospitals is, in some cases, expensive or “immoral”. One possible alternative is to keep them at home while ensuring care, comfort and safety. To reach such an objective, we propose an approach which is based on the multi agent nets architecture for modelling and simulating different services of an elderly smart home (security, comfort and economy services). The aim is to restore independent living at home for people who should normally be placed in health care institutions.

articleTitle: Random Pixel Selection through Image Cropping for Data Augmentation and Classification
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Data augmentation is one of the strategies addressing the challenge of lack of data, which constitutes an obstacle to getting high accuracy during training Deep Neural Networks. Through this paper, we propose a new method based on the random selection of pixels by cropping some rows and columns from a given image to create new images with a reduced number of pixels. It allows the creation of images with new rows and columns which differ from the original image. This assures enriching and diversifying the original dataset while trying to capture the regions of interest and dismiss the other regions, which leads to better generalization of the training model, The accuracy of the proposed method on Deep Convolution Neural Network applied to the Kaggle Cat VS Dog dataset achieves 77.05% with 40000 samples, whereas the accuracy when applied the original dataset (with 10000 samples) was 73.65%.

articleTitle: Introducing Generative adversarial networks on Estimation of distribution algorithm to solve permutation-based problems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: As a subclass of evolutionary algorithms, estimation of distribution algorithms (EDAs) have found widespread use in a variety of optimization problems with impressive performance. In each generation, they build a probabilistic model representing the promising individuals, and the next generation constructs by sampling this model. Constructing and sampling the probabilistic model is a real challenge in developing such algorithms. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are a popular kind of generative model that has been widely adopted due to their ability to generate new samples that closely match the distribution of training data. However, research on how GANs handle permutation spaces is lacking. We suggest a novel Estimation of Distribution Algorithm (EDA) that uses GANs as a probabilistic model estimator to advance this subject. in order to preserve the information captured from the selected individuals, those promising individuals were represented by a one-hot matrix, then used to train GANs. The proposed algorithm is tested to solve two permutation problems: The Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP) and Permutation Flowshop Scheduling Problem (PFSP). The Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can obtain the optimal solution in some instances and a near-optimal in others.

articleTitle: Block-based copy-move forgery detection in digital images: a survey
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Digital photographs are employed in a variety of settings, including crime scene investigation, forensic analysis, and courts. With the introduction of image editing tools, modifying and manipulating image content has become a breeze. Nowadays, anyone with minimal computer skills may readily edit or delete significant image data without leaving apparent evidence. Image forgeries can be done in several methods, including copy-move and splicing. Given the seriousness of these alterations, it is critical to detect any picture manipulation properly. Several approaches for detecting copy-move forging (CMFD) have been developed. These approaches are categorised as block-based (BLK) or keypoint-based (KP). This paper provides an overview of recent research papers on CMFD published in prestigious conferences and journals.

articleTitle: On the use of Blockchain Technology in Supply Chains: A brief review
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Recently, The application of Blockchain technology in supply chains has drawn more attention from researchers and increased due to its ability to provide transparency, tracking, tracing, security and enhance confidence and trust among the members participating in the supply chain. In this paper, we provide a brief review which focuses on the use of the Blockchain technology to tackle with three challenges which are facing supply chains, namely traceability, trust and digitization. Besides, the paper provides a discussion about some sectors where the Blockchain technology is adopted at an advanced stage.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-based 3D-GAN for Glioma Subregions Detection and Segmentation in Multimodal Brain MRI volumes
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Accurate, fast, and automatic gliomas segmentation from brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans is crucial for brain cancer diagnosis and therapy, but it remains, until nowadays, challenging because of variations in location, form, and imaging intensity of gliomas. This paper presents an automatic high- and low-grade glioma (HGG and LGG) sub-regions segmentation technique using deep learning-based three-dimensional generative adversarial network (3D-GAN) that localizes and segments the whole gliomas and their intra-regions, comprising necroses, edemas and active tumors, in multimodal brain MRI volumes of BraTS'2022 Datasets. Experimental tests and evaluations of the proposed GAN model have been realized on both, BraTS'2022 training and validation datasets, containing 5880 brain MRIs corresponding to 1470 different subjects with HGG and LGG of various sizes, forms, locations, and intensities. Dice coefficients for enhancing tumor (ET), whole tumor (WT), and tumor core (TC) reached 0.770, 0.872 and 0.832 respectively on 20 % of the training dataset. On the challenge validation dataset, our model achieved an average ET, WT, and TC Dice score of 0.774, 0.907 and 0.829 respectively.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerance Optimization of Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems: Multi-objective Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm for Process Planning
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: A reconfigurable manufacturing system (RMS) is a modern manufacturing system class that aims to provide functionality and capacity as and when needed. Reconfigurable machine tools (RMTs) are the main component of RMS, which have a modular structure, such that they can be reconfigured into different configurations. In RMSs, process planning aims to assign to each operation the appropriate configuration. During the fulfillment of operations along the process plan, RMTs may defect. Monitoring the state of RMS during process planning allows for diagnosing the defect of broken-down components. After detecting the defect, the repairing team of the company is responsible for repairing this defect. Furthermore, periodic maintenance for the system components is required for facilitating the monitoring of RMS. The accomplishment of all steps of each process, i.e., monitoring, maintenance, and repairing, requires time and a specific cost. This paper deals with the problem of maximizing fault-tolerance optimization in RMSs. A multi-objective optimization model is proposed considering the minimum total time and minimum total cost of process plans incorporating repair time of configurations and maintenance cost of configurations, during the process planning. This problem represents an NP-hard problem, for solving it, the multi-objective artificial bee colony (MOABC) algorithm is adapted to generate a set of non-dominated solutions (i.e., process plans). With the help of a numerical example, the results obtained by MOABC are compared with a well-known meta-heuristic algorithm, called non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGA-II), and demonstrated the superiority of MOABC over the NSGA-II in terms of solution quality, convergence, and solutions' diversity.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques for Predicting Heart Diseases
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is another term for heart disease, refers to a variety of heart-related illnesses and has been the leading cause of death in recent decades. In the healthcare industry, data mining is a typical tool for evaluating enormous amounts of data. Wide variety of data mining and machine learning methods were used to analyze large amounts of complex medical data, assisting healthcare providers in identifying heart diseases. This works aims to used Sequential Minimal Optimization (SOM), Naive Bayesian, Random Forest, Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), Multilayer Perceptron, Adaboost, and Logistic Regression as classifiers and evaluate it accuracy with Heart Stalog Dataset. To improve performance of the selected classifiers Harmony Search Algorithm (HSA) was used as effective features selection tools. Feature selection is a key topic for dimension reduction and classification in high-dimensional datasets. During the feature selection procedure, only the most relevant attributes from the datasets will be chosen. The results show the accuracy was enhanced in Random Forest from 87.037% and AdaBoost from 84.0741% to 92.123% and 94.234 % respectively after using HSA on least number of attributes.

articleTitle: KEDAS: A validated Arabic Speech Emotion Dataset
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: This paper aims to construct and validate Arabic emotional speech data for speech emotion recognition systems. This work took place in two main phases: collecting, evaluating, and validating audio data according to human perception. Then the data is processed in terms of framing, normalisation, and background denoising to make the data accessible to models of emotion recognition systems. The result of this work is a KasdiI-Merbah Ouargla University Dataset(Kedas Dataset) for emotional speech in standard Arabic language, which includes 5000 audio recording files distributed to emotions of anger, happiness, sadness, fear and neutrality. A total of 10 of the most used phrases in communication are based on literary and scientific studies. Five hundred actors from the university community recorded the data (students, professors and staff), and fifty-five others evaluated the validity of the identification and the reliability, including Arabic linguists, literary researchers, and specialists in clinical psychology.

articleTitle: Leveraging Formal Methods to Blockchain Consensus Protocols: A Scoping Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Recently, the concept of blockchain has emerged and caused a stir in the digital world and this translates into a new perspective on the security, flexibility, and efficiency of systems. To solve various problems that exist in Byzantine environments the blockchain uses consensus algorithms to solve these problems. These consensus algorithms are essential to ensure long-term stability in a blockchain system, so consensus forms the basis of blockchain technology. Therefore, the appearance of a set of consensus protocols aims to improve the efficiency of blockchain systems and meet the individual needs of different application areas. On the other hand, to make blockchain platforms more secure and reliable for information sharing, and an optimal solution for value transfer, formal methods have been used to provide sufficient mathematical proofs to ensure user safety and security. In this paper, a scoping literature review on leveraging formal methods to consensus protocols is presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Support vector machine based clustering: A review
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Clustering is one of the most important data mining techniques, its objective is to regroup similar objects into groups, with the aim of maximizing the intra-cluster similarit and minimizing the inter-cluster similarity in unsupervised way. Recently, support-based clustering methods attracted a lot of attention, especially Support Vector Clustering (SVC) due to its capability to overcome the main hardships of classical clustering methods. SVC can easily handle complex shape clusters and identify their number without initialization. SVC undergoes on two main steps, training and labeling, the first one consist of solving a quadratic programming problem (QPP) to obtain a decision mathematics function, which is used in the next step to label all objects with their appropriate clusters. However, training an SVC model (solving a QPP) and labelling objects using huge data sets can lead to a high computation burden, in order to surmount this main issue and trying to improve the SVC performance, many methods and techniques was proposed in literature. In this paper, we aim to highlight and classify some of the most insightful works proposed by researchers according to their targeted SVC step.

articleTitle: The use of Deep Learning techniques in E-Learning systems and MOOCs
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: E-Learning and Massive Open Online Courses are old techniques, but since the Coronavirus, they have become more popular again. Students already suffer from a lack of concentration and motivation in traditional courses; thus, this lack affects online courses. Furthermore, another important Online Learning systems problem is the difference between learners in terms of Learning Styles, abilities, social characteristics as well as preferences, background, and other psychological and mental features. Generally, these features are not taken into account by scientists. Therefore, Deep Learning techniques and Datasets have been used to improve E-Learning systems and MOOCs in several aspects such as: predicting dropout, Learning Styles and performance of online learners, and even their attention after taking an online course. In this work, we have studied and analyzed many recent works in the area of using Deep Learning techniques to improve Online Learning systems and MOOCs. This analysis shows what researchers rely on to improve E-Learning and MOOCs and demonstrates that research does not use the definition of the appropriate Learning Style frequently. However, the most used ones are dropout and performance of learners. In another hand, learners' attention is still gap.

articleTitle: AI Technologies for Predicting and Preventing Road Accidents - A Review
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Nowadays, researchers are attempting with all the available technologies to offer a resolution to the problems of road accidents that cause of death of many people every day, for several reasons. The existing efforts are focused on the vehicle's safety through the development of several tools and applications based on artificial intelligence that aims to ensure safety in every way. This study is conducted as part of the efforts to contribute to reducing the incidence of road accidents due to their negative human and material effects on society in all areas, by investigating the various research attempts that have been carried out to apply different artificial intelligence technologies such as maching learning, Internet of things, and Multi-agent systems with the spread of the use of modern communications media via wireless networks. In this paper, we study the latest research efforts that are concentrated on developing preventive and prediction solutions to solve road accident problems using smart infrastructure devices such as semaphores, sensors, and cameras with intelligent and statistical methods.

articleTitle: Usability evaluation from client-side traces using heatmap and system usability scale
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: In this project, we investigate the usability of a gamified application developed as part of the e-learning system for the University of Souk Ahras. The online application is integrated within the university web portal, allowing students and lecturers to ask questions and receive answers from other students or lecturers within the university about any modules. This would result in creating a knowledge base of questions and answers for every module that future students could benefit from without the need to ask their lecturers again. We propose the use of heat maps for assessing usability based on client-side traces where a JavaScript app is used to track user behaviors while exploring the university website remotely without accessing or modifying the main university website. The suggested tool is integrated into the webpage by inserting a single line of JavaScript code. After logging and storing the data, a heat map is generated from this data using PHP and JavaScript to assess the most active areas where users payattention when interacting with the website. Furthermore, we created an online implementation of the System Usability Scale questionnaire in order to assess the satisfaction of university participants in using the Question Board platform. The SUS is considered after using the platform. For users who couldn't manage to use the application, we have devised a special questionnaire. Finally, a questionnaire is devised for users who haven't used the application in order to figure out the main reasons for the weak turnout on the platform

articleTitle: Intelligent Farm Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning for optimal control
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: Smart agriculture is the use of automation, sensors, and data to improve crop yields, reduce costs and increase crop quality. Predictive analytics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence are used. Another benefit of using artificial intelligence in agriculture is the ability to optimize the consumption of resources such as water and fertilizer to achieve the greatest yield. However, to date, the technology has not been used to optimize the management of agricultural operations. The objective of this paper is to introduce the concept of smart farming and discuss applying deep reinforcement learning for optimal management in the field. We propose a smart farming system that uses Deep Reinforcement Learning to optimize the operation of a farm. The system uses Deep Learning to recognize patterns in a large dataset of real-world agricultural data, such as crop yields and weather, and uses this knowledge to recommend actions. It also dynamically learns optimal control policies for a variety of crops, depending on the farmer's goals and current conditions.

articleTitle: Simulation and Formal Verification in WSNs Empowered by Machine Learning: A Review
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on iNnovative Informatics of Biskra (ISNIB)
abstract: The performance analysis of the protocols that were designed in WSNs can be conducted either using simulation or through formal verification. The ability of simulations and formal methods to specify and verify WSNs has attracted the attention of many researchers. Since these methods are practically based on state space exploration, they face some scalability issues when the defined system has a high density, which is frequently the case for WSNs. Machine learning (ML) techniques can be used to address this issue. ML is the technique that automatically learns from data and acts without re-program or human intervention. Applying ML in WSNs to improve the performance of these networks consists of using the historical data obtained by simulation or formal verification with the aim of predicting the future state of the deployed network to limit human intervention. This work reviews recent research works that applied ML techniques in many domains, and after that, works that exploited ML-based algorithms in WSNs are explored. Finally, we present a discussion on open issues.
